constantine-petros.outcome: Four of the five charges against Constantine William Petros were dismissed in 2017. The remaining charge resulted in a conviction after a no-contest plea. On September 17, 2020, the court reduced the offense to a misdemeanor, granted dismissal under Penal Code § 1203.4 and terminated probation. This was post-conviction relief, not an acquittal.

brief.allegation: The five filed counts alleged conspiracy, insurance-claim misconduct, and grand theft. Filing charges was not a finding that each allegation was true.
brief.disposition: Four counts were dismissed in March 2017. A no-contest plea on the remaining insurance-claim count led to a conviction recorded in July 2017.
brief.sentence: The court imposed five years of formal probation in July 2017 and recorded its termination on September 17, 2020. The reviewed docket does not establish whether any custodial time was actually served.
brief.later: On September 17, 2020, the remaining count was reduced to a misdemeanor and dismissed under Penal Code §1203.4; probation was terminated. This was not an acquittal or a finding of factual innocence.
